pr_title: add skylint check for missing rule documentation
pr_comments:
Note that there's now a doc attribute:
```
new_rule = rule(
  implementation = _new_rule_impl,
  attrs = {
    "foo": attr.label(),
    "bar": attr.string(),
  },
  doc = """some documentation"""
)
```

So maybe we should recommend that instead of a docstring?
you are right. I forgot this attribute. I will change it to use the doc attributes of the rules and their attributes.

issue_context.title: skylint does not check missing rules docstring
issue_context.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

skylint does not check for missing docstring of rules.

### Feature requests: what underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?

public variables of type rule and repository_rule should throw an error like:
`rule 'foo' has no docstring [missing-rule-docstring]`

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

skylint should not pass on:
```python
"""foo"""

def _impl(ctx):
    print("foo", ctx.attr.bar)

foo = rule(
    _impl,
    attrs = {
        "bar": attr.string(),
    },
)
```

### skylint from Bazel version

0.11.1
comments: We're going to retire Skylint in favor of Buildifier (https://github.com/bazelbuild/buildtools).

review_comments: Why the new newline parse logic?

Ok, I see. Can you add a short comment right above the if, explaining that this catches the case where the first line is empty? That'll make it easier to follow this function's logic alongside the above and below comments.
So we're requiring function docstrings to be non-empty, but not rule/attr docstrings?
i could add a check for empty string  rule/attr docstrings. @brandjon what do you think?

If we're going to prohibit empty docstrings then let's be consistent for other kinds of objects.

Can you use the error() helper instead of constructing DocstringParseError directly?

So this now raises an Issue?

    def foo():
        """
        Does a foo.
        """

This seems like a separate stylistic discussion that should be in another PR. Is there any corresponding github issue / consensus?
i uses the format of skydoc (https://skydoc.bazel.build/docs/writing.html). the doc format should be matching.
In that case, can we change "the one-line summary is missing" to "docstrings must begin with a one-line summary (with no preceding newline)"? That way we avoid a confusing error message in this case.
i think its for the missing one-line summary

Ok, now I see. The -1 is there to get the last column on the line (inclusive), and the `max(1, ...)` ensures this can't cause it to dip down to col 0, which doesn't exist, in the case that the line is empty. Your change generalizes this to also work when it's the first line that is empty (where startColumn isn't 1), so that in that case we still get a proper issue rather than what I presume is a stack trace due to a bad LocationRange.
Same issue, no need for the docstring to be literal here. Note that Stardoc (Skydoc renamed) will actually evaluate the code to extract the dynamically produced docstring value.
